segments.t: Arriving in the northern town of Bergues, Andrea pays an unexpected visit to Dany Boon's mother, Madame Bonnero. Andrea hopes to preserve the agency's bond with the star, but Madame Bonnero insists on hospitality first. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Bonjour, je cherche Madame Bonnero.
Oui, c'est moi, qui êtes-vous?
Je viens vous parler de Dany.
Je ne parle jamais aux journalistes.
Je ne suis pas une journaliste!
Qui êtes-vous alors, jeune femme?
Entrons, je vous explique tout.
Venez dans ma cuisine chaleureuse.
Chez ASK, on connaît bien Dany.
Mathias s'occupait toujours de lui.
Mathias a abandonné le navire.
Prenez le temps et mangez bien.
Je veux bien prendre mon temps.
Alors, qu'est-ce qu'on mange ensemble?
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Bonjour, je cherche Madame Bonnero.
'Hello, I am looking for Madame Bonnero.' Andrea arrives at the front door. The verb 'look for' means to look for someone or something.
Oui, c'est moi, qui êtes-vous?
'Yes, that is me, who are you?' Madame Bonnero greets the visitor cautiously. The tonic pronoun 'me' is used after c'est.
Je viens vous parler de Dany.
'I come to speak with you about Dany.' Andrea states the reason for her trip. The verb 'come' is followed by an infinitive to express purpose.
Je ne parle jamais aux journalistes.
'I never talk to journalists.' Madame Bonnero expresses her distrust of the media. The negative adverb 'never' indicates not at any time.
Je ne suis pas une journaliste!
'I am not a journalist!' Andrea clarifies her professional background. The feminine indefinite article 'a' agrees with journaliste.
Qui êtes-vous alors, jeune femme?
'Who are you then, young woman?' Madame Bonnero asks for her true identity. The adverb 'then' marks a logical transition.
Entrons, je vous explique tout.
'Let's go in, I explain everything.' Andrea suggests talking inside. The imperative 'let's enter' proposes entering together.
Venez dans ma cuisine chaleureuse.
'Come into my warm kitchen.' Madame Bonnero welcomes Andrea into her home. The adjective 'warm' describes a welcoming atmosphere.
Chez ASK, on connaît bien Dany.
'At ASK, we know Dany well.' Andrea underscores the agency's closeness with the star. The preposition 'chez' denotes at the premises of.
Mathias s'occupait toujours de lui.
'Mathias always took care of him.' Madame Bonnero remembers the former agent fondly. The reflexive verb 's'occuper de' means to look after someone.
Mathias a abandonné le navire.
'Mathias abandoned ship.' Andrea uses a vivid metaphor for his sudden departure. The noun 'ship' evokes a seafaring vessel.
Prenez le temps et mangez bien.
'Take the time and eat well.' Madame Bonnero dispenses motherly wisdom. The imperative 'take' encourages slowing down.
Je veux bien prendre mon temps.
'I really want to take my time.' Andrea accepts the pause from agency stress. The phrase 'prendre son temps' means to unhurry.
Alors, qu'est-ce qu'on mange ensemble?

'So, what do we eat together?' Madame Bonnero prepares a generous northern meal. The interrogative pronoun 'qu'est-ce que' asks about the food. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Andrea discovers the generous hospitality of Dany Boon's mother in Bergues. By sharing a simple meal, she begins rebuilding trust to protect the agency. Now, let's review the scene one last time.
